recipes.name: Grilled Corn Salad
ingredients_raw: 0.5 bunch fresh cilantro, chopped, or more to taste
2 teaspoons olive oil, or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Roast corn on the preheated grill, turning occasionally, until tender and specks of black appear, about 10 minutes. Remove from the grill and let sit until just cool enough to handle, 5 to 10 minutes.
Holding a corn cob over a large bowl, use a knife to carefully slice warm kernels directly into the bowl; discard cob. Repeat with remaining corn.
Add bell pepper, tomatoes, onion, cilantro, olive oil, salt, and pepper; toss until evenly mixed. Let sit until flavors have blended, at least 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Corn Salad
raw_recipe.description: This easy grilled corn salad is packed with roasted corn, fresh veggies, and cilantro for a colorful side dish perfect for any BBQ or summer day.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make a quick and easy colorful salad perfect for the summer. The base of the salad is sweet grilled corn. It's combined with tomatoes, peppers onion and fresh cilantro and simply dressed with olive oil, salt and pepper.

review.reviewBody: Overall, very good! Plus it's a great way to use up leftover grilled corn. I subbed cucumber for the green pepper as a personal preference. And I definitely agree with some of the other reviewers that this needs lime juice. I also added a bit of sugar to the "dressing" and let this set in the fridge for a few hours to let the flavors blend together. Very simple, very tasty and bursting with color!

This was good and I will make it again but with the following changes:
add 2 avocados, juice of one whole lime, a 1/2 teaspoon of cumin and a smashed clove of garlic.
I let the favors meld overnight. Make sure you add enough salt and pepper as it really needs it. 
This was turned it up a notch!

This is a very good recipe especially with fresh corn arriving in our Texas grocery stores currently. I left out the green bell pepper and added fresh lime juice based on other reviews and since I brushed the ears of corn with olive oil prior to roasting I found that the dish did not need the 2 tsp. of olive oil. Also, just because I was in a hurry, I used a corn holder in the end of the cob to aid in cutting the kernels from the cob while they were still hot. It also helped to cool the corn down faster so that the remaining ingredients could be added. All in all this great recipe for all that summer corn that’s here and more on it’s way. I will definitely be using this recipe again. Thanks Amber.
Really good! I substitute the olive oil for the juice of one lime, which balances the sweet corn really well.

Like others, I used lime juice instead of olive oil. Trader Joe's has grilled green olives, and I sliced and used those for some additional fat instead of olive oil. I also used a little bit of cumin and a little more paprika. Since I was taking this to a potluck with a varied group, I swapped Italian/flat parsley for the cilantro. It was a very nice substitution. Two frozen bags of roasted corn were perfect for me who was short on time and short of a grill. I will gladly use this for future picnics. It's nice to have a recipe that doesn't need to be kept cold at an outdoor event.

Grilled the jalapeño, tomato and onion to add a little more smoke. Squeeze of lime and some salt really made it pop. Didn't have cojeta cheese so I used feta. A great bite and contrast to the sweet corn. This is super fast and tasty

It was delicious almost immediately but even better when I let it marinade for 2 days. I used red peppers instead of green (personal preference) and added just a bit more sugar. Great for camping because I made it ahead of time.

I didn't have the ears of corn or the green peppers but I took frozen corn and "grilled" them in my cast iron skillet with a tiny bit of EVOO. It toasted and grilled them perfectly! I then added it to the remainer of the ingredients in my salad bowl, garnished with cilantro. YUM! Too bad the portions are too small. I would double, even triple the recipe!

I used frozen corn and put everything on aluminum foil and on the grill. Worked fine, but I think my grill was a little too hot. Charred on the edges and not in the middle. I'll definitely make this again.
Very good, added lime & roasted the corn w/ butter, paprika & S&P. Will add either feta or quesa fresco next time for some additional depth.

Love grilled corn! I added an avocado, and mixed about 2 T lime juice, 1 T sugar, and about 1/4 C Olive oil for the 'dressing'. I also sprinkled with Queso Fresco because cheese. The grilled corn flavor was awesome, and the avocado added creaminess. I'll definitely make this again!
Both red onion and green bell pepper are strong-flavored, too biting for this sweet corn recipe. Substituting Vidalia onion and red bell pepper might tone it down a notch to make it tastier.
Everything about this is so delicious!!!!!
Good Recipe

I really like this salad. A nice change to the traditional pasta salads at outdoor gatherings. I will definitely keep making it every summer. Everyone in my family loves this salad. It makes a great light lunch for meal prep too.
I threw in some black beans to make it a high protein meal for my girlfriend and I. Both of us loved it.
Lime juice in the dressing makes this a lot better. Otherwise there no acidity really.

We enjoy this in the summer. I normally cook the corn in the microwave if we aren't grilling. I also add green onions instead of the red onions at times. Along with other reviewers, we also add a bit of lime juice to the recipe. It's fresh and speaks perfectly to summer.
Quite good! Squeezed in some fresh lime juice and it really did the trick. Yum! So fresh and light …a keeper.

This is a fabulous recipe. It is very versatile, and you can pretty much modify the veggies based on what you have on hand. The corn and tomatoes should probably remain as the base ingredients, though.I made with frozen/thawed fire-roasted corn, and grape tomatoes quartered.I agree with others that a spritz of lime juice takes it up a notch.
